questions.question: In May 2025, which among the following institutions formally announced the creation of the Payments Regulatory Board (PRB), a six-member panel responsible for overseeing the country’s payment systems?

options.text: Securities and Exchange Board of India
Small Industries Development Bank of India
National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Reserve Bank of India**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** announced the formation of the **Payments Regulatory Board (PRB)** in May 2025. The PRB is a six-member panel entrusted with the responsibility of overseeing and regulating the country's payment systems.
 
• The **Payments Regulatory Board** was established as per the recommendations of the **Committee on Digital Payments**, headed by **Ratan Watal**. This committee emphasized the need for a separate regulatory body for payment systems in India.
 
• The PRB's objectives include ensuring the development of secure, efficient, and accessible payment systems while promoting innovation and competition in the payment ecosystem.
 
• The six-member PRB comprises the **Governor of the RBI** as the Chairperson, a Deputy Governor of the RBI as a member, and nominees from the Central Government, along with independent experts in the field of payment systems.
 
• The establishment of the PRB aligns with the RBI's role in fostering a robust and secure digital payment infrastructure, which is critical for the country's digital economy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Reserve Bank of India (RBI):**

 
 
• The **Reserve Bank of India** is India's central bank, established on **April 1, 1935**, under the **Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934**.
 
• It is headquartered in **Mumbai**, Maharashtra, and primarily functions to regulate the issue of currency and manage the country's monetary policy.
 
• The RBI plays a crucial role in supervising and regulating banks, fostering financial stability, and promoting the development of financial markets.
 
 
 
• **Committee on Digital Payments:**
 
 
• The **Ratan Watal Committee** was constituted by the Government of India in **2016** to suggest measures to increase the use of digital payments.
 
• It recommended the establishment of a dedicated regulatory body for payment systems to ensure better governance and oversight.
 
 
 
• **Functions of the Payments Regulatory Board:**
 
 
• Regulating payment systems in India to ensure their security, efficiency, and accessibility.
 
• Promoting competition and innovation in the payment ecosystem.
 
• Ensuring the protection of consumer interests in the digital payment space.
 
• Monitoring the compliance of payment service providers with regulatory norms and guidelines.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Payment Systems Regulation:**
 
 
• A robust payment system infrastructure ensures **secure and efficient transactions**, fostering trust in the digital economy.
 
• Regulation helps in mitigating risks such as **frauds, cyberattacks, and operational failures** in payment systems.
 
• It promotes financial inclusion by enabling easier access to digital payment methods for underserved populations.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The RBI is responsible for overseeing the country's payment systems under the **Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007**.
 
• The establishment of the PRB was a significant step to ensure the growth of a **secure, seamless, and innovative payment ecosystem** in India.
 
• The PRB's formation reflects India's commitment to strengthening its digital payment infrastructure, which is pivotal to achieving a **cashless economy**.
 
• Global examples, such as the **Payment Systems Regulator (PSR)** in the UK, have demonstrated the benefits of having a separate regulatory body for payment systems.

questions.question: Which of the following states launched Surakshit Shanivar (Safe Saturday), a disaster preparedness initiative for students in June 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bihar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Surakshit Shanivar (Safe Saturday)** is a disaster preparedness initiative launched by the state of **Bihar** to educate students about disaster management and response strategies.
 
• This initiative was introduced in **June 2025** to address the state's vulnerability to natural disasters such as floods, earthquakes, and cyclones.
 
• The program aims to enhance the **disaster resilience** of students by providing them with practical training, mock drills, and awareness sessions.
 
• By focusing on school children, the initiative seeks to build a culture of preparedness and safety among the younger generation.
 
• The program aligns with the state's efforts to reduce disaster risks and ensure **sustainable development** by incorporating disaster education into the academic curriculum.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Natural Disasters in Bihar:**

 
 
• Bihar is highly prone to natural disasters such as **floods**, which occur annually due to overflowing rivers like the Ganga, Kosi, and Gandak.
 
• The state also experiences **earthquakes** as it lies in the seismic zone V and IV, making it highly vulnerable to seismic activities.
 
• Cyclones and droughts are other significant challenges faced by the region, affecting agriculture and livelihoods.
 
 
 
• **Disaster Preparedness in India:**
 
 
• The **National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA)** was established in 2005 under the **Disaster Management Act** to coordinate disaster preparedness and response.
 
• India has implemented various programs like the **National Cyclone Risk Mitigation Project** (NCRMP) and the **Earthquake Risk Mitigation Project** to reduce vulnerabilities.
 
 
 
• **Role of Schools in Disaster Preparedness:**
 
 
• Schools play a critical role in disaster preparedness by educating children about **risk reduction** and emergency response.
 
• Programs like **mock drills**, evacuation exercises, and first-aid training empower students to act effectively during emergencies.
 
 
 
• **Key Initiatives by Bihar:**
 
 
• Bihar has implemented several disaster preparedness programs, including flood forecasting systems and community-based disaster management training.
 
• The state government actively collaborates with organizations like the **UNICEF** and the **National Institute of Disaster Management (NIDM)** to enhance disaster resilience.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Disaster Management Act, 2005:**

 
 
• This act provides the framework for disaster risk reduction, preparedness, and response in India.
 
• It mandates the establishment of the **NDMA** at the national level and the **State Disaster Management Authorities (SDMAs)** at the state level.
 
 
 
• **UN Sendai Framework (2015-2030):**
 
 
• The Sendai Framework emphasizes the importance of **disaster risk reduction** through education, capacity building, and community participation.
 
• India is a signatory to this framework and incorporates its principles into national disaster management policies.

questions.question: Which of the following folk artists became the first dhaki to win a Padma Shri in 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gokul Chandra Das**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Gokul Chandra Das**, a renowned **dhaki artist**, became the first dhaki to receive the prestigious Padma Shri award in **2025**. This recognition highlights the contribution of traditional folk art to India's cultural heritage.
 
• A **dhaki** is a traditional drummer who plays the **dhol**, especially during the festival of **Durga Puja** in West Bengal and other parts of eastern India. Their rhythmic beats are an integral part of the festive celebrations.
 
• Gokul Chandra Das was honored for his exceptional dedication to preserving and promoting the **art of dhaki drumming**, which has been a part of India's intangible cultural heritage for centuries.
 
• The Padma Shri award, India's **fourth-highest civilian honor**, is given for distinguished contributions in various fields, including art, literature, sports, and social work.
 
• This award has brought attention to folk artists who often remain underrepresented despite their significant contributions to India's cultural fabric.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Padma Awards:**

 
 
• The Padma Awards are one of the highest civilian honors in India, instituted in **1954**. They include Padma Vibhushan, Padma Bhushan, and Padma Shri.
 
• The awards are conferred by the President of India and recognize excellence in various fields such as **art, literature, social work, public affairs, science, and sports**.
 
• Padma Shri is awarded for distinguished contributions, and recipients are selected through nominations vetted by committees.
 
 
 
• **Dhaki Tradition:**
 
 
• Dhakis are traditional drummers, primarily found in **West Bengal, Odisha, and Assam**. They play the **dhol**, a large drum, during various celebrations, especially **Durga Puja**.
 
• The beats of dhakis serve as a call to devotees during religious ceremonies and create a festive ambiance.
 
• Dhakis often wear traditional attire and perform synchronized movements while drumming, adding to the visual appeal of their performance.
 
 
 
• **Durga Puja:**
 
 
• Durga Puja is a major Hindu festival celebrated across India, especially in **West Bengal**. It marks the victory of Goddess Durga over the demon Mahishasura.
 
• The festival is characterized by grand decorations, idol worship, cultural performances, and the rhythmic beats of dhakis.
 
• Dhaki drummers play a pivotal role in enhancing the spiritual experience of the festival through their vibrant and energetic beats.
 
 
 
• **Recognition of Folk Artists:**
 
 
• Folk artists contribute significantly to preserving India's **intangible cultural heritage**. Their recognition through awards like Padma Shri helps in promoting and safeguarding these traditions.
 
• Such honors bring attention to marginalized communities and encourage younger generations to continue practicing traditional art forms.
 
• Artists like Gokul Chandra Das serve as **ambassadors of cultural heritage**, inspiring others to appreciate and sustain India's rich traditions.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Leander Paes:** An Indian tennis legend known for his numerous Grand Slam victories and contributions to Indian sports. However, he is not associated with dhaki drumming or Padma Shri for folk art.
 
• **Mary Kom:** A celebrated Indian boxer and Olympic medalist, known for her achievements in sports. She is unrelated to the folk art of dhaki drumming.
 
• **Anant Nag:** A veteran Indian actor known for his work in Kannada cinema, but he has no association with the traditional art of dhaki drumming.

questions.question: Where was the 2ⁿd Global Cervical Cancer Elimination Forum held?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bali, Indonesia**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **2nd Global Cervical Cancer Elimination Forum** was held in **Bali, Indonesia**, emphasizing the importance of eliminating cervical cancer as a public health issue globally.
 
• The forum focused on strategies to achieve the **World Health Organization's (WHO) global strategy** for eliminating cervical cancer through vaccination, screening, and treatment.
 
• It brought together global health experts, policymakers, researchers, and organizations to discuss advancements and challenges in combating cervical cancer.
 
• The event highlighted the importance of **HPV vaccination programs** and accessible cervical cancer screening methods, particularly in low- and middle-income countries.
 
• The forum also stressed the need for **equitable healthcare access** and international collaboration to eradicate cervical cancer by 2030.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Human Papillomavirus (HPV) and Cervical Cancer:**

 
 
• **HPV** is the main cause of cervical cancer, with types 16 and 18 responsible for nearly 70% of cases globally.
 
• Vaccination against HPV is a key preventive measure, with vaccines like **Gardasil** and **Cervarix** widely used.
 
• Regular screening methods, such as **Pap smears** and **HPV DNA testing**, help in the early detection and treatment of precancerous lesions.
 
 
 
• **WHO Global Strategy for Cervical Cancer Elimination:**
 
 
• Launched in **November 2020**, the strategy aims to reduce cervical cancer cases and deaths by promoting vaccination, screening, and treatment.
 
• The goal is to achieve **90% HPV vaccination coverage**, **70% screening coverage**, and **90% access to treatment** for cervical cancer globally.
 
• The strategy also emphasizes public awareness campaigns and strengthening healthcare systems.
 
 
 
• **Bali, Indonesia:**
 
 
• Bali is a popular global destination known for its **cultural heritage**, **natural beauty**, and as a center for international conferences and forums.
 
• The selection of Bali for the forum highlights Indonesia's commitment to advancing global health initiatives and fostering international collaboration.
 
 
 
• **Global Impact:**
 
 
• Cervical cancer is the **fourth most common cancer** among women worldwide, with over **600,000 new cases** and **340,000 deaths** annually.
 
• Forums like this are critical in addressing disparities in healthcare access, especially in **low-income** and **developing countries**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Global Statistics:**

 
 
• Cervical cancer accounts for about **7.5% of all female cancer deaths** globally.
 
• It is highly preventable through **vaccination** and **early detection**.
 
 
 
• **HPV Vaccination Programs:**
 
 
• Several countries have implemented **national HPV vaccination programs** targeting adolescents to prevent cervical cancer.
 
• Vaccination coverage is improving, but challenges remain in ensuring equitable access.
 
 
 
• **Role of International Collaboration:**
 
 
• Forums like the **Global Cervical Cancer Elimination Forum** play a crucial role in fostering partnerships and sharing best practices.
 
• Global organizations like **WHO** and **UNICEF** are key stakeholders in these initiatives.
 
 
 
• **Indonesia's Healthcare Initiatives:**
 
 
• Indonesia has been actively working to improve healthcare access and outcomes through programs focusing on vaccination, maternal health, and cancer prevention.
 
• The forum in Bali underscores the country's dedication to global health priorities.

questions.question: Who is the author of the book ‘Wild Fictions: Essays’ published in January 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Amitav Ghosh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Amitav Ghosh** is a renowned Indian author known for his significant contributions to literature, particularly in the fields of fiction and essays.
 
• The book "**Wild Fictions: Essays**" published in **January 2025** is attributed to Amitav Ghosh, showcasing his expertise in blending environmental and cultural themes.
 
• Amitav Ghosh's works often focus on issues such as **climate change, colonialism, and historical narratives**, making him a prominent voice in contemporary literature.
 
• His previous works include critically acclaimed books such as "**The Great Derangement**" and "**The Glass Palace**", which explore themes of human interactions with nature and history.
 
• Ghosh has been the recipient of several prestigious awards including the **Jnanpith Award**, India’s highest literary honor, for his contribution to literature.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **About Amitav Ghosh:**

 
 
• Born on **July 11, 1956**, in Kolkata, India, Amitav Ghosh has established himself as a global literary figure.
 
• He holds academic qualifications from **St. Stephen's College, Delhi University**, and a doctorate from **Oxford University**.
 
• His writing style often intertwines **historical fiction** with modern-day concerns, particularly focusing on **global environmental issues**.
 
 
 
• **Key Themes in “Wild Fictions: Essays”:**
 
 
• The book explores the concept of **wildness** in nature and its intricate connection with human civilization.
 
• It delves into topics such as **climate change, ecological degradation, and the human role in altering natural landscapes.**
 
• Ghosh’s essays provide a unique perspective on literature’s role in addressing global environmental challenges.
 
 
 
• **Other Works by Amitav Ghosh:**
 
 
• **The Great Derangement**: A non-fiction work focusing on the impact of **climate change** and its representation in literature.
 
• **Sea of Poppies**: A historical novel exploring the lives of characters impacted by the **opium trade** during the British colonial era.
 
• **Gun Island**: A novel with themes of migration and environmental crises.
 
 
 
• **Global Recognition:**
 
 
• Amitav Ghosh has received international accolades such as the **Prix Médicis étranger** and has been shortlisted for the **Booker Prize**.
 
• His works have been translated into several languages, enabling his ideas to reach a global audience.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Environmental Literature:** Amitav Ghosh is regarded as a pioneer in addressing **climate change** and ecological themes in fiction, a genre that has gained prominence in recent years.
 
• **Contributions to Indian Literature:** His works have significantly contributed to the global recognition of **Indian authors** in the literary community.
 
• **Legacy:** Ghosh’s influence extends beyond literature, inspiring discussions on the **intersection of culture, history, and environmental sustainability.**
 
• **Book Release:** The publication of "**Wild Fictions: Essays**" in January 2025 is expected to attract readers interested in **ecological narratives and literary essays.**

• The establishment of the board aims to promote turmeric cultivation, improve its marketing strategies, and address the concerns of turmeric farmers.

• It is known for its various applications in **cooking, medicine, cosmetics, and dyeing**.
 
• Indian turmeric is highly sought after in international markets for its superior quality and **high curcumin content**.

• It aims to create a centralized system for managing turmeric production, quality control, and export logistics.
 
• It will also facilitate **scientific research** to improve the yield and quality of turmeric crops.
 
 
 
• **Turmeric's Importance:**
 
 
• Turmeric has significant **medicinal properties**, including anti-inflammatory and antioxidant effects.
 
• It is a key ingredient in traditional Indian medicine systems like **Ayurveda** and **Siddha**.
 
• The global demand for turmeric has increased due to its use in health supplements and natural remedies.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Turmeric Export:**

• The establishment of the National Turmeric Board will help streamline the export process and improve the global competitiveness of Indian turmeric.
 
 
 
• **Government Initiatives:**
 
 
• The Indian government has launched various schemes to support spice farmers, such as **Mission for Integrated Development of Horticulture (MIDH)**.
 
• These initiatives aim to enhance the productivity and profitability of spice cultivation, including turmeric.

• It is designed to carry both fixed-wing aircraft like the Rafale-Marine and rotary-wing aircraft for various operational roles.
 
• Equipped with modern sensors and weapons, it enhances India’s capability to project power in the **Indian Ocean Region**.
 
• The addition of Rafale-Marine jets will significantly bolster INS Vikrant’s operational efficiency.

questions.question: In 2025, Shubhanshu Shukla conducted an International Space Station (ISS) experiment with moong and methi seeds to study:

options.text: Soil nutrient cycling under space conditions
Resistance of legumes to common pesticides

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Seed germination under microgravity conditions**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Seed germination under microgravity conditions** was the focus of Shubhanshu Shukla's experiment in 2025 on the International Space Station (ISS).
 
• The study aimed to understand how seeds like **moong** (green gram) and **methi** (fenugreek) germinate in the absence of Earth's gravity.
 
• Microgravity poses unique challenges for biological processes such as seed germination, including issues like **water distribution, nutrient absorption, and root growth orientation**.
 
• Understanding seed behavior in space is critical for the development of **space farming**, a necessary step for long-term human space exploration and colonization.
 
• This experiment contributes to the field of astrobiology and sheds light on the viability of growing food in extraterrestrial environments. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Microgravity and Its Effects:**

 
 
• Microgravity is a condition where objects appear to be weightless and experience minimal gravitational force. It is common in space.
 
• Under microgravity, water tends to form spherical droplets, and nutrient distribution becomes uneven, which can complicate plant growth.
 
 
 
• **Space Farming:**
 
 
• Space farming involves growing crops in extraterrestrial environments, such as the ISS or other planets like Mars.
 
• It is essential for providing a sustainable source of food for astronauts on long-duration missions.
 
• Plants also contribute to life support systems by producing oxygen and removing carbon dioxide.
 
 
 
• **Moong and Methi Seeds:**
 
 
• **Moong** (green gram) is a protein-rich legume widely used in Indian cuisine.
 
• **Methi** (fenugreek) is known for its nutritional and medicinal properties, including its ability to reduce blood sugar levels.
 
• Both are fast-growing plants, making them ideal for short-term experiments like those conducted on the ISS.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Seed Germination Studies in Space:**
 
 
• Understanding seed germination in space helps scientists design systems for growing crops in extraterrestrial environments.
 
• It also contributes to our understanding of how plants adapt to extreme conditions, which can have applications on Earth, such as in arid or nutrient-poor soils.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Challenges in Space Farming:**

 
 
• Watering plants in microgravity is difficult as water does not flow naturally but instead forms floating droplets.
 
• Lack of soil in space requires innovative techniques like hydroponics or aeroponics for plant growth.
 
• Light exposure in spacecraft is artificial, requiring the use of LED systems to simulate sunlight.
 
 
 
• **Previous Experiments:**
 
 
• NASA has conducted experiments on growing crops like lettuce, radishes, and wheat aboard the ISS.
 
• The European Space Agency (ESA) has also studied plant growth under simulated Martian and lunar conditions.
 
 
 
• **Future Implications:**
 
 
• Successful space farming can reduce the dependency on Earth for food supplies during space missions.
 
• It can also pave the way for establishing self-sustaining human colonies on planets like Mars.
 
 

``

__
 
• **Technology Development Board (TDB)** signed an agreement with **APChemi Pvt. Ltd., Navi Mumbai**, in **February 2025** to produce purified pyrolysis oil for making circular plastics and sustainable chemicals.
 
• **APChemi Pvt. Ltd.** specializes in converting waste plastics into **high-value pyrolysis oil**, which can be further refined into sustainable chemicals and circular plastics.
 
• The collaboration aims to bolster the **circular economy** by promoting the reuse of plastic waste, reducing environmental pollution, and supporting sustainable industrial practices.
 
• Purified pyrolysis oil is a critical feedstock for creating **low-carbon plastics** and sustainable chemical solutions, aligning with India’s **green and environmental goals**.
 
• Through this agreement, the initiative aims to reduce the dependency on fossil fuel-based feedstocks in the production of plastics and chemicals, promoting the use of **recycled materials**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **APChemi Pvt. Ltd.**:

 
 
• Headquartered in **Navi Mumbai**, this company is a leading technology provider in the field of **waste plastic pyrolysis**.
 
• It operates advanced pyrolysis facilities that transform **non-recyclable plastic waste** into purified pyrolysis oil, which can be used in various industrial applications.
 
• APChemi has gained recognition for its **cutting-edge technology** and its commitment to sustainability and reducing plastic waste.

• Its primary mission is to promote the development and commercialization of indigenous technology solutions in India.
 
• It provides financial assistance to industries and enterprises for innovative and environmentally sustainable projects.
 
 
 
• **Pyrolysis Technology:**
 
 
• Pyrolysis is a **thermal decomposition** process that converts organic materials, such as plastic waste, into useful by-products like **pyrolysis oil**, char, and syngas.
 
• The process operates at high temperatures in the absence of oxygen, ensuring that the materials break down into smaller molecules.
 
• Purified pyrolysis oil is increasingly being used as a **feedstock** for producing sustainable chemicals and circular plastics.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Circular Plastics:**

• This approach helps in mitigating **plastic pollution** and contributes to achieving **climate goals** by lowering greenhouse gas emissions.
 
• The use of circular plastics supports the **United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)**, particularly those related to responsible consumption and production.

• **India’s Defence Manufacturing Sector:**

 
 
• The Indian government has introduced several reforms to promote **indigenous defence production**, such as increasing the **FDI limit to 74%** through the automatic route.
 
• Key initiatives like **‘Atmanirbhar Bharat’** and the **Defence Production and Export Promotion Policy (DPEPP) 2020** aim to enhance the domestic defence manufacturing ecosystem.
 
• India’s defence exports have witnessed a significant rise, with the government targeting **₹35,000 crores in exports by 2025**.
 
 
 
• **Slovakia’s Defence Industry:**
 
 
• Slovakia is renowned for its expertise in manufacturing **land-based defence systems**, including **infantry fighting vehicles, mortars, and radar systems**.
 
• The country is a member of **NATO** and the **European Union**, which ensures that its defence manufacturing standards align with global benchmarks.
 
• Slovakia’s defence exports are primarily focused on Europe, the Middle East, and now, emerging markets like India.
 
 
 
• **Significance of India-Slovakia Defence MoU:**
 
 
• The agreement is expected to enhance **India’s technological capabilities** in the defence sector by accessing Slovakia’s advanced military technologies.
 
• It provides a platform for **joint development and production**, ensuring that India can cater to its defence needs while also contributing to global markets.
 
• The partnership signifies India’s growing focus on establishing **strategic collaborations** with European nations to diversify its defence partnerships.
 
 
 
• **JCBL Group:**
 
 
• The **JCBL Group**, a leading Indian company, specializes in **automotive and defence manufacturing**, including armoured vehicles and other military hardware.
 
• The group has been instrumental in facilitating international collaborations to bring advanced technologies to India.
 
• Its role in this MoU underscores the importance of public-private partnerships in achieving India’s defence production goals.

• **‘Make in India’ Initiative:**

 
 
• Launched in **2014**, this initiative aims to transform India into a global manufacturing hub by encouraging both foreign and domestic companies to manufacture in India.
 
• In the defence sector, it emphasizes **self-reliance**, with policies designed to reduce imports and promote indigenous development.
 
• As part of this initiative, the government has identified **101 defence items** for indigenization.
 
 
 
• **Defence Collaboration with Other Nations:**
 
 
• India has signed similar defence agreements with countries like **Israel** (for UAVs and radar systems) and **Russia** (for BrahMos missile systems).
 
• These partnerships have significantly contributed to India’s defence capabilities and export potential.
